articles.title: Grid Stencil Mesh
articles.summary: Coarse woven stencil grid with recessed cells and bridge tabs; strong micro sparkle, directional sheen. Reads as a fine square mesh or screen grid; on metal a regular checked-tile texture, on satin a dotted lattice of bright corner squares.
articles.what: Grid Stencil Mesh assembles stencil cell frames, stencil bridge tabs, recessed grid corners, registration chevrons and overspray edge grains. Up close: A strict square grid of about 30 px cells, each framed in a thin line with a little V-shaped chevron mark and a small solid square tab at one corner. Square corner tabs flare as bright pixel blocks on satin; on metal the frames and chevrons read as crisp check-mark tiles. From a distance: Reads as a fine square mesh or screen grid; on metal a regular checked-tile texture, on satin a dotted lattice of bright corner squares. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Track & Motorsport (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Track & Motorsport", or search for "Grid Stencil Mesh".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: the grid needs open panels to stay regular
Apply to flat sections where distortion is low
Numbers keep their colour; the grid adds visible but light texture behind them, legibility stays good.
Bright corner-square dots in the highlight over a faint grid; pixel-screen look
Pairs well with: matte, gloss, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a check or plaid colour pattern: it adds no colour, only shine change
Not carbon fibre: cells have chevron marks and corner tabs, no weave
Avoid: too fine at distance, overwhelms small panels.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
